t: This is Hoxton Square, a public garden square in Hackney, laid out in 1683 and thought to be one of the oldest in London. Since the 1990s it has been the heart of Hoxton's arts and media scene, and the tall Victorian buildings around it now hold bars, restaurants, offices and a live music club. Two people were born here. John Thomas, born in 1805, became the founder of the Christadelphian movement and wrote Elpis Israel. Charles Le Cren, born in 1831, later became a public servant in the colony of Victoria.
